blocks.explanation:
A product of an algebraic and a logarithmic function.
Plan: take \(\ln x\) as the first function (ILATE: L before A) and \(x^7\) as the second, then integrate by parts once.
steps:
Given: \(\int x^7\ln x\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: integration by parts with \(f(x) = \ln x\), \(g(x) = x^7\), because \(\ln x\) becomes \(\frac{1}{x}\) and \(x^7\) is easy to integrate.

Integrate the second, differentiate the first
\[\int x^7\,dx = \dfrac{x^8}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln x = \dfrac{1}{x}\]
Why: power rule \(\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\).

Apply integration by parts
\[= \ln x\cdot\dfrac{x^8}{8} - \int \dfrac{x^8}{8}\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{1}{8}\int x^7\,dx\]
Why: \(\frac{x^8}{x} = x^7\); the constant \(\frac{1}{8}\) comes outside.

Integrate
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{1}{8}\cdot\dfrac{x^8}{8} + c\]
\[= \dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8} - \dfrac{x^8}{64} + c\]
Why: \(\int x^7\,dx = \frac{x^8}{8}\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^8\ln x}{8}\right) = x^7\ln x + \dfrac{x^7}{8}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^8}{64}\right) = \dfrac{x^7}{8}\]
Why: the \(\frac{x^7}{8}\) terms cancel, leaving \(x^7\ln x\).
